title: Morocco vs Egypt: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Morocco and Egypt based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 🍲 Food & Dining
categories.summary: This is Morocco's knockout category. Moroccan cuisine is widely considered one of the finest in Africa and the Middle East, and Reddit travelers consistently rave about it. categories.title: 🏛️ History & Culture
categories.summary: Egypt's ancient heritage is in a category of its own. The Pyramids of Giza are the last surviving Wonder of the Ancient World, and standing at their base is one of those rare travel moments that genuinely lives up to the hype. categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Egypt is significantly cheaper than Morocco across nearly every category. The Egyptian pound has devalued dramatically (from 15 EGP/$1 in 2022 to ~48 EGP/$1 in 2026), making Egypt one of the cheapest tourist destinations in the world for Western visitors. Morocco is still affordable compared to Euro

categories.title: 🚌 Getting Around
categories.summary: Morocco has a solid transport network. The ONCF trains connect major cities (Casablanca–Marrakech: 2.5h, $10–15; Casablanca–Fez: 3h, $15–25), and the Al Boraq high-speed train between Tangier and Casablanca takes just 2 hours. CTM and Supratours buses cover routes the trains don't, including desert
redditQuotes: In Egypt, get Uber. Seriously. It was a game-changer compared to dealing with taxi drivers. In Morocco, the petit taxis are fine — just make sure they use the meter outside of Marrakech."—r/travel use

categories.title: 🏨 Where to Stay
categories.summary: Marrakech— The main event for most first-timers. Stay in the medina for the full immersion (riads around Jemaa el-Fna or the quieter Mouassine quarter), or in Gueliz/Hivernage for modern hotels and easier navigation. Riads range from $30–50 (basic) to $150–400+ (luxury with pools and rooftop dining)

categories.title: 🎒 Day Trips
categories.summary: Both countries have excellent day trip potential from their main bases, but the experiences are very different.

categories.title: 🔀 Why Not Both?
categories.summary: Unlike Tokyo and Kyoto (2 hours apart by bullet train), Morocco and Egypt are separated by 3,500+ kilometers of North Africa. faqs.question: Is Morocco or Egypt better for first-time visitors to North Africa?
faqs.answer: Morocco is generally considered easier for first-time visitors to North Africa. It has better tourist infrastructure, more diverse landscapes within a compact area, and the hassle from touts is widely reported as less intense than in Egypt. Egypt, however, offers once-in-a-lifetime ancient monuments

faqs.question: Which is cheaper to visit, Morocco or Egypt?
faqs.answer: Egypt is significantly cheaper. A mid-range daily budget in Egypt runs $60-100 USD per person, while Morocco costs $80-150 USD per person per day. Egypt accommodation, food, and transport are roughly 30-40% cheaper. However, Egypt major archaeological sites have raised entrance fees dramatically.

faqs.question: Is Morocco or Egypt safer for tourists?
faqs.answer: Both countries are generally safe for tourists, with low risk of violent crime. The main safety concern in both is aggressive touts and scam attempts, which are widely reported as worse in Egypt (especially Cairo and Luxor). Morocco hassle is concentrated in Marrakech medina but is milder in cities

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Morocco vs Egypt?
faqs.answer: For Morocco: 10-14 days is ideal to see Marrakech, Fez, the Sahara, Chefchaouen, and either the coast or Atlas Mountains. A minimum of 7 days covers Marrakech, Fez, and a Sahara excursion. For Egypt: 7-10 days covers Cairo/Giza, Luxor, Aswan, and optionally Abu Simbel or the Red Sea.

faqs.question: Which has better food, Morocco or Egypt?
faqs.answer: Reddit overwhelmingly favors Moroccan food. Morocco cuisine is widely considered one of the best in Africa and the Middle East with tagines, couscous, pastilla, and harira soup. Egyptian food is hearty and affordable (koshari, ful medames, shawarma) but less diverse. Egypt wins on sheer affordabilit

faqs.question: Can you visit both Morocco and Egypt in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it is a long trip. Direct flights between Casablanca and Cairo take about 5 hours and cost $200-400 USD round trip. For a combined trip, plan at least 2.5-3 weeks. Most travelers choose one per trip since both countries offer enough to fill 10-14 days on their own.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Morocco and Egypt?
faqs.answer: Both countries share similar optimal seasons. The best time for Egypt is October through April when temperatures are bearable. For Morocco, March through May and September through November offer the best weather. Morocco summers are brutal inland but pleasant on the coast.
